record_status: CANDIDATE — not written to the project database
PHENOMENON: Endogenous single-error restoration: a one-bit DATA lesion of either codeword is detected, localized, corrected by exactly one toggle, and the auxiliary organization then returns to baseline.
DOMAIN: Specimen A (4 DATA + 17 AUX Boolean coordinates), strict synchronous update, fan-in <= 2; authorized P-DATA (8) and P-FULL single-coordinate perturbations (42).
INITIAL_CONDITIONS: x in R_X = B_H(0000,1) U B_H(1111,1), q = q* = 0^17; or a codeword full state with one coordinate flipped.

LOCAL_RULES.D: d_ij' = x_i XOR x_j for (i,j) in {12,13,23,14,24}

CAUSAL_MECHANISM: Syndrome decoding of the [4,1,4] repetition code: D computes parity checks (target-blind, complement-invariant); E marks the unique coordinate that disagrees with both of its witnesses; L delays E by one step so that P is the rising edge of E; P toggles the marked coordinate once. Direction = location (from E) x binary toggle of the current value; the majority bits carry the basin identity and are never read as a value.
NECESSARY_CONDITIONS: each of the 17 auxiliaries and each of the 21 gates (single ablations and all 267 gate replacements fail the battery)
x -> D transmission (EXP-03), P -> X action edge (EXP-01)
one-step memory L for the rising-edge gate (without it: linear GF(2) loop, 15- or 7-cycles)
auxiliary state at or near q* when the lesion arrives; at most one correction in flight (second lesion at t1-t3 can enter a 12-cycle)
the single pulse must act (no retry: P(restore) = 1 - pulse loss)
SUFFICIENT_CONDITIONS: the frozen rules from (x in R_X, q*): restoration of x at t4 and of the full 21-bit state at t7 (8/8)
downstream of detection: one correct E event (D amputated) restores x (8/8)
physically: one correct P event (E amputated) restores x, but the location then comes from outside (8/8)
FACILITATORS: linearity of the code: the syndrome depends only on the error, not on the codeword
balanced pipeline: every x -> D -> E path has length 2
triangle + pendant witness graph: resolves all weight-2 ties (12 of 48 five-detector assignments do)
INHIBITORS: pulse loss or actuator ablation (latched alarm)
stuck-at DATA faults (one pulse spent, alarm latched)
mixed-family double perturbations (x+e, x+p, e+p) on two distinct triangle coordinates, e.g. x1+e2 (12-cycle; 36 of the 420 double flips; same-coordinate mixtures and those touching x4 return)
a second DATA error while a correction is in flight

FAILURE_BOUNDARY.DATA: weight-2 states (exact tie set of the code): resolved by triangle majority, not by nearest codeword
FAILURE_BOUNDARY.full_state: 38.57% of the 2^21 states reach a target; 60.50% six 12-cycles; 0.93% fourteen latched-alarm fixed points
FAILURE_BOUNDARY.perturbation_radius: all 42 single flips return; 366/420 double flips return

INVARIANTS: global complement of x commutes with G (all 2^21 states)
(x1 x2) with induced relabelling is an automorphism
q trajectories identical for complementary lesions; I(q_t; codeword) = 0
exactly one E and one P pulse per P-DATA trajectory
l(t) = e(t-1); p(t+1) = e(t) AND NOT e(t-1)
COUNTEREXAMPLES: single-witness locator: false toggle of a healthy bit that stays latched
4-detector cycle witness graphs: valid on R_X but all 6 weight-2 states latch
6 of 30 six-detector witness assignments cycle on weight-2 starts
SCALE_VERIFIED: N=4 exhaustively; the specimen-A architecture for n = 3..8: every single error restored with DATA at t4 and full state at t7; the final codeword from q* is the triangle majority for all 2^n x.
SCALE_PREDICTED: Mathematical radius t = floor((n-1)/2); any one-shot restoring decision needs essential arity >= 2t+1 (proved; brute-force checked for n=4,5,6), hence fan-in-2 depth >= ceil(log2(2t+1)). The specimen-A architecture keeps radius 1 at every n; radius >= 2 needs new locators (not built).
FORMAL_LAW: s(t+1)=Hx(t); eps_i(t+1)=s_{i,a}(t) AND s_{i,b}(t); pi(t+1)=eps(t) AND NOT eps(t-1); x(t+1)=x(t) XOR pi(t). From (x0,q*): x(4) = x0 XOR eps(H x0), x_i(4) = maj(x_i, x_a(i), x_b(i)); on R_X, Phi(x) = argmin_c d_H(x,c).
